(1) For the city, the city police chief or, in the absence of the police chief, the second in command designated by written authorization of the police chief.

(Code 2011, § 30-82)
981:
(a) To invoke mutual aid under the provisions of the mutual aid agreement between the city and county, the designated official from the requesting law enforcement agency shall be required to contact the designated official from the responding law enforcement agency by telephone or in writing. The responding law enforcement agency may request such information from the requesting law enforcement agency as is necessary to confirm the emergency situation, and to assess the types and amounts of assistance that shall be provided.
(b) During an emergency situation, all personnel from responding agencies shall report to and shall work under the direction and supervision of the designated supervisor of the requesting agency at the site; provided, however, that at all times officers shall adhere to the policies and procedures of their own department, and shall only be required to respond to lawful orders.
(c) Personnel responding to a call for mutual aid outside of their appointed jurisdiction shall have those law enforcement powers as are provided by state law.
(d) In the event of a mutual aid request involving actual or potential mass arrest, the responding law enforcement officers shall only make arrests for offenses directly related to the incident and shall assist in the processing of arrestees as follows:
(1) Identification of arrestees;
(2) Control of property obtained from arrestees;
(3) Completion of arrest certificates;
(4) Transportation of arrestees; and
(5) Court duty pertaining to arrests.
(e) In any emergency situation in which mutual aid has been requested, radio communications should be established between all of the parties, where possible, through the use of the local public mutual aid radio system.
(f) The governing authorities of the city and county, when providing mutual aid personnel, are each responsible for the wages, pension, and workers' compensation benefits of their own personnel as a result of the emergency situation.
(g) Each governing authority shall be responsible for maintaining and providing to each other on a regular basis an accurate account of available resources including, but not limited to, available personnel per shift, equipment, and specialized units.
(h) Each governing authority shall develop and update on a regular basis a plan providing for the effective mobilization of all its resources and facilities to cope with any type of emergency situation.
(i) Mutual aid operational plans shall be developed and updated on a regular basis by the governing authorities and are operative between them in accordance with the provisions of such plan.
(j) The governing authorities shall meet on a regular basis to review all mutual aid plans and the provisions of this article.
(Code 2011, § 30-83)

Manufactured or mobile homes on separate, individual lots, subject to the requirements of these regulations, shall be allowed in residential zoning district R-2.
(1) On separate lot. Only one manufactured or mobile home shall be located on each individual lot, parcel, or tract, except in an approved manufactured or mobile home park. No manufactured or mobile home shall be located permanently on any plot, parcel, or tract of land occupied by any other permanent dwelling or occupied building.
(2) Compliance with district zoning. Manufactured or mobile homes on individual lots shall fully comply with the zoning district's requirements for lot size, setbacks, and other restrictions for permanent single-family residential dwellings, as well as the requirements of these regulations.
(3) Minimum site improvements. Manufactured or mobile homes on separate, individual lots shall be provided with the following minimum improvements to the manufactured or mobile home and lot:
a. Each manufactured or mobile home shall be supported by a permanent concrete block or brick foundation, fully closed and vented; or the base of the manufactured or mobile home shall be fully skirted to screen the manufactured or mobile home supports or wheels from view. Acceptable skirting shall be only those types and materials designed by the manufacturer expressly for such use on manufactured or mobile homes.
b. Each manufactured or mobile home shall be served by an acceptable water supply and method of sewage disposal subject to the written approval of the local health authority having jurisdiction over such matters.
c. Each manufactured or mobile home shall have an individual connection to public electrical power.
d. Each manufactured or mobile home lot shall contain at least two off-street parking spaces.
e. Any accessory structures or additions to the manufactured or mobile home or lot shall be of a similar design and material as the manufactured or mobile home unit, and shall not be used as complete, independent housing units with permanent provisions for sleeping, cooking, and sanitation.

(a) It shall be unlawful and it is hereby declared to be a nuisance for any person to park or let stand any private or commercial vehicle upon any premises to which the public has access, without the owner's permission, including, but not limited to, such premises as shopping center parking lots, church parking lots, service station parking lots, private business establishment parking lots, and private individuals' driveways within the city between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. each night, where the vehicle's presence upon the premises is unrelated to the normal activity, use or business for which the premises are made available to the public, and when:
(1) The owner of the premises has made a dedication of his premises to the city for the limited purpose of enforcement of this section;
(2) The owner of the premises has made a written request to the city that the provisions of this section be enforced as to his premises; and
(3) The owner of the premises has erected, at his expense, signs on his premises giving notice to the public in substantially the following form:
"No parking or loitering is allowed on these premises between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. by order of the police department of the City of Cochran."
(b) Whenever any vehicle shall be found on any premises within the city in violation of the provisions of this section, such vehicle may be removed by any member of the police department by means of towing it, or otherwise, to a vehicle pound. It is the intent of the city council that nothing in this division shall be construed to abrogate or impair the powers of the courts or of any department of the city to enforce any provisions of any local enabling act or ordinance or regulation, nor to prevent or punish violations thereof; and the powers conferred by this article shall be in addition to and supplemental to the powers conferred by any other law or ordinance, legislation, or regulation.

1017:
The public officers designated herein may issue citations for violations of state minimum standard codes, optional building, fire, life safety, and other codes adopted by ordinance, and conditions creating a public health hazard or general nuisance, and may seek to enforce such citation in a court of competent jurisdiction prior to issuing a complaint in rem, as provided in this section.
(Code 2011, § 34-73)
1018:
(a) It is the duty of the owner of every dwelling, building, structure, or property within the jurisdiction to construct and maintain such dwelling, building, structure, or property in conformance with applicable codes in force within the city, or such ordinances which regulate and prohibit activities on property and which declare it to be a public nuisance to construct or maintain any dwelling, building, structure or property in violation of such codes or ordinances.
(b) The city council hereby appoints or designates the city marshal, city fire chief, city police chief, building inspector, and their designees as public officers to exercise the powers prescribed by this section.
(Code 2011, § 34-74)
1021:
Complaints issued by a public officer pursuant to this division shall be served in the following manner. In all cases, a copy of the complaint and summons shall be conspicuously posted on the subject dwelling, building, or structure within three business days of filing of the complaint and at least ten days prior to the date of the hearing. A copy of the complaint and summons shall be served in one of the following ways:
(1) Personal service upon each owner and party in interest, if such parties are residents of the county. Service shall be perfected at least ten days prior to the date of the hearing. Service may be made by the public officer designated by ordinance to abate nuisances or by any law enforcement officer of the city; and a return of service, filed with the clerk of the appropriate court, shall be deemed sufficient proof that service was perfected pursuant to state law or statutory overnight delivery.
(2) If any owner or party in interest is a resident of the state but resides outside of the county, service shall be perfected by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested, to the most recent address shown in the county tax filings and mailed at least 14 days prior to the date of the hearing.
(3) Nonresidents of the state, whose mailing address is known, shall be served by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested, mailed at least 14 days prior to the date of the hearing. For nonresidents whose mailing address is unknown, a notice stating the date, time, and place of the hearing shall be published in the newspaper in which the sheriff's advertisements appear in such county once a week for two consecutive weeks prior to the hearing.
(4) In the event either the owner or any party in interest is a minor, an estate, an incompetent person, or a person laboring under disabilities, the guardian or other personal representative of such person shall be served, and such guardian or personal representative resides outside of the county or is a nonresident of the state, he shall be served as provided for in this section. If such owner or party in interest has no guardian or personal representative, service shall be perfected by serving the judge of the probate court of the county wherein such property is located at least 30 days prior to the date of the hearing, which judge shall stand in the place of and protect the rights of such minor, estate, or incompetent person, or appoint a guardian ad litem for such person.
(5) In the event of unknown persons or unborn remaindermen who are likely to have any rights in the property or interest or the proceeds thereof, the judge of the probate court of the county wherein such property or interest is located shall be personally served at least 30 days prior to the date of the hearing, and it shall be the duty of the judge of the probate court to stand in the place of and protect the rights of such unknown parties or unborn remainder-men.
(6) In the event the whereabouts of any owner or party in interest is unknown and the same cannot be ascertained by the public officer in the exercise of reasonable diligence or if any owner or party in interest cannot, after due diligence, be served as provided herein, the public officer shall make an affidavit to that effect, and serve by publication in the manner provided herein, and such publication shall be sufficient proof that service was perfected.
(Code 2011, § 34-77)
1022:
Orders and other filings made subsequent to service of the initial complaint shall be served in the manner provided in this division on the owner and any party in interest who answers the complaint or appears at the hearing. Any party who fails to answer or appear at the hearing shall be deemed to have waived all further notice in the proceedings.
(Code 2011, § 34-78)
1023:
A notice of lis pendens shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the superior court in the county in which the dwelling, building, or structure is located at the time of filing the complaint in the appropriate court. Such notice shall have the same force and effect as other lis pendens notices provided by law.
(Code 2011, § 34-79)
1024:
(a) Whenever a request is filed with the public officer by a public authority or by at least five residents of the city charging that any dwelling, building, or structure:
(1) Is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes;
(2) Is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or
(3) Constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions.
the public officer shall make an investigation or inspection of the specific dwelling, buildings, structure, or property. If the officer's investigation or inspection identifies that any dwelling, building, structure, or property is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the public officer may either issue a citation to the property owner in the same manner as for a traffic violation or other offense in municipal court or, alternatively, issue a complaint in rem against the lot, tract, or parcel of real property on which such dwelling, building, or structure is situated or where such public health hazard of general nuisance exists, and shall cause summons and a copy of the complaint to be served on the owner and parties in interest in such dwelling, building, or structure.
(b) The complaint shall identify the subject real property by appropriate street address and official tax map reference; identify the owner of the parties in interest; state with particularity the factual basis for the action; and contain a statement of the action sought by the public officer to abate the alleged nuisance.
(c) The summons shall notify the owner and parties in interest that a hearing will be held before a court of competent jurisdiction as determined by O.C.G.A. § 41-2-5, at a date and time certain and at a place within the city where the property is located. Such hearing shall be held not less than 15 days nor more than 45 days after the filing of said complaint in court. The owner and parties in interest shall have the right to file an answer to the complaint and to appear in person or by attorney and offer testimony at the time and place fixed for hearing.
(d) If after such notice and hearing, the court determines that the dwelling, building, or structure in question is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use and is not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the court shall state, in writing, findings of fact in support of such determination, and shall issue and cause to be served upon the owner and any parties in interest that have answered the complaint or appeared at the hearing, an order determining the following:
(1) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, buildings, or structure can be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to repair, alter, or improve such dwelling, building, or structure so as to bring it into full compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violation and, if applicable, to secure the structure so that it cannot be used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or
(2) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, building, or structure, in order to bring it into full compliance with applicable codes relevant to the cited violations, cannot be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to demolish and remove such dwelling, building, or structure and all debris from the property.
(e) For purposes of this section, the court shall make its determination of reasonable cost in relation the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure without consideration of the value of the land on which the structure is situated; provided, however, that costs of the preparation necessary to repair, alter, or improve a structure may be considered. Income and financial status of the owner shall not be a factor in the court's determination.
(f) The present value of the structure and the costs of repair, alteration, or improvement may be established by affidavits of real estate appraisers with a state appraiser classification as provided in O.C.G.A. § 43-39A-24, qualified building contractors, or qualified building inspectors, without actual testimony presented. Costs of repair, alteration, or improvement of the structure shall be the cost necessary to bring the structure into compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violations in force in the jurisdiction.
(Code 2011, § 34-80)
1025:
(a) If the owner fails to comply with an order to repair or demolish the dwelling, building, or structure, the public officer may cause such dwelling, building, or structure, to be repaired, altered, improved, vacated and closed, or demolished. Such abatement action shall commence within 270 days after the expiration of time specified in the order for abatement by the owner. Any time during which such action is prohibited by a court order issued pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 41-2-13 or any other equitable relief granted by a court of competent jurisdiction shall not be counted toward the 270 days in which such abatement action must commence. The public officer shall cause to be posted on the main entrance of the building, dwelling, or structure a placard with the following words:
"This building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business use and does not comply with the applicable codes or has been ordered secured to prevent its use in connection with drug crimes or constitutes any endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions. The use or occupation of this building is prohibited and unlawful."
(b) If the public officer has the structure demolished, reasonable efforts shall be made to salvage reusable materials for credit against the cost of demolition. The proceeds of any moneys received from the sale of salvaged materials shall be used or applied against the cost of the demolition and removal of the structure, and proper records shall be kept showing the application of sales proceeds. Any such sale of salvaged materials may be made without the necessity of public advertisement and bid. The public officer and the city are relieved of any and all liability resulting from or occasioned by the sale of any such salvaged materials, including, without limitation, defects in such salvaged materials.
(Code 2011, § 34-81)
1026:
(a) The amount of the cost of demolition, including all court costs, appraisal fees, administrative costs incurred by the tax counselor, attorney's fees, and all other costs necessarily associated with the abatement action, including restoration to grade of the real property after demolition, shall constitute a lien against the real property upon which such costs were incurred.
(b) The lien provided for in this section shall attach to the real property upon the filing of a certified copy of the order requiring repair, closure or demolition in the office of the clerk of the superior court in the county and shall relate back to the date of the filing of the lis pendens notice pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 41-2-12.
(c) The clerk of the superior court shall record and index such certified copy of the order in the deed records of the county and enter the lien on the general execution docket.
(d) The lien shall be superior to all other liens on the property, except liens for taxes, to which the lien shall be inferior, and shall continue in force until paid.
(e) After filing a certified copy of the order with the clerk of the superior court, the public officer shall forward a copy of the order and a final statement of costs to the county tax commissioner. It shall be the duty of the county tax commissioner to collect the amount of the lien in conjunction with the collection of ad valorem taxes on the property and to collect the amount of the lien as if it were a real property ad valorem tax, using all methods available for collection of real property ad valorem tax, including specifically O.C.G.A. § 48-4-1 et seq.; provided, however, that the limitation of O.C.G.A. § 48-4-78 which requires 12 months of delinquency before commencing a tax foreclosure shall not apply.
(f) The tax commissioner shall remit the amount collected to the governing authority of city. Thirty days after imposition of the lien, the unpaid lien amount shall bear interest and penalties in the same amount as applicable to interest and penalties on unpaid real property ad valorem taxes.
(g) The tax commissioner shall collect and retain an amount equal to the cost of administering a lien hereunder unless such costs are waived by resolution of the county. Any such amount collected and retained for administration shall be deposited in the general fund of county to pay the cost of administering the lien.
(h) The city may waive and release any such lien imposed on property upon the owner of such property entering into a contract with the county or municipality agreeing to a timetable for rehabilitation of the real property of the dwelling, building, or structure on the property and demonstrating the financial means to accomplish such rehabilitation.
(Code 2011, § 34-82)
1027:
Where the abatement action does not commence in the superior court, review of a court order requiring the repair, alteration, improvement, or demolition of a dwelling, building, or structure shall be by direct appeal to the superior court under O.C.G.A. § 5-3-29.

1030:
The following acts are prohibited and are declared to be public nuisances:
(1) The making, creating or permitting of any excessive, unreasonably loud, or unnecessary noise in the city is prohibited.
(2) The making, creating or permitting of any such noise, sound or vibration of such intensity, duration, frequency or character which would be harmful and detrimental to the health, welfare and safety of the inhabitants of the city is prohibited.
(Code 2011, § 34-110)
1031:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully make or continue or cause to be made or continued, any loud, excessive, unnecessary, or unusual noise which disturbs the peace or quiet of any neighborhood or which causes discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal sensitiveness residing in the area, which would include business areas, as well as public streets and sidewalks.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully make or continue or cause to be made or continued, any loud, excessive, unnecessary or unusual noise by or within a motor vehicle which disturbs the peace or quiet of any neighborhood or which causes discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal sensitiveness in the area, which would include business areas, as well as public streets and sidewalks. Included within this restriction are loud or no mufflers on motor vehicles and sound reproduction or amplification equipment in or on motor vehicles such as radios, tape or cassette players and megaphones, as well as any other device that transmits sound.
(c) For purposes of this section, excessive noise shall include, but is not limited to, sound from any source which registers 85 decibels or more on a sound level meter or other instrument designed to measure sound level. For noises or sound created inside a building or dwelling, the same shall be measured at the property line of that building or dwelling. For purposes of motor vehicles, sound or noise shall be measured ten feet from such motor vehicle.
(d) In addition to the other restrictions and standards contained in this section, it shall be unlawful for any person operating or occupying a motor vehicle on a public street or other public property or other property used by the public to operate or amplify with sound produced by a radio, tape player, or other mechanical sound-making device or instrument from within the motor vehicle so that the sound is plainly audible at a distance of 100 feet or more from said motor vehicle. The term "plainly audible" is defined as any excessive, loud unnecessary, or unusual noise which disturbs the peace or quiet of any neighborhood or which causes discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal sensitiveness residing in the area which includes the business area as well as public streets and sidewalks in the city. This prohibition is in addition to, and not exclusive of, the other provisions of this chapter.
(e) The provisions of this section shall not apply to any law enforcement or emergency vehicle in the performance of lawful duties or to the noise made by a horn or other warning device as required by O.C.G.A. § 40-8-70, or to any motor vehicle used for business or political purposes which, in the normal course of such business, uses sound-making devices.
(Code 2011, § 34-111)

1126:
The governing authorities of the city and the county have found it necessary, desirable, and in the public interest to establish a formal process for resolving land use disputes as they relate to property annexation and land use plans. This article is intended to establish that process and, to that end, the city and county have adopted similar provisions.
(Code 2011, § 42-40)
1127:
(a) Prior to initiating any formal annexation activities, the municipality will notify the county of a proposed annexation and provide information on location of property, size of area, and proposed land use or zoning classification, if applicable, of the property.
(b) Within 30 days following receipt of the information required in subsection (a) of this section, the county will forward to the city a statement indicating that the county has no objection to the proposed land use for the property or describing its bona fide objection to the city's proposed land use classification, providing supporting evidence, and listing any possible stipulations or conditions that would alleviate the county's objections.
(c) If the county has no objection to the city's proposed land use or zoning classification, the city is free to proceed with the annexation. If the county fails to respond to the city's notice in writing within the deadline, the city is free to proceed with the annexation and the county loses its right to invoke the dispute resolution process, or object to land use changes after the annexation.
(d) If the county notifies the city that it has bona fide land use classification objections, the city will respond to the county in writing within 30 days of receiving the county's objections by either:
(1) Agreeing to implement the county's stipulations and conditions, thereby resolving the county's objection;
(2) Agreeing with the county and stopping action on the proposed annexation; or
(3) Disagreeing that the county's objections are bona fide, in which event the city will initiate a joint meeting of the respective governments to resolve the issue.
(e) If the city initiates mediation, the city and the county will agree on a mediator, mediation schedule and determine participants in the mediation. The city and county agree to share equally any costs associated with the mediation.
(f) An annexation proposal shall not be effective until any bona fide land use classification objections raised by the county are resolved pursuant to the dispute resolution process.
(g) The final resolution of any recommendation of a land use classification will be accorded to the governing body considering the annexation. In cases of land use disputes not related to annexation proposals, the final resolution of a land use dispute will be accorded to the jurisdiction in which the subject property is located. Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, either local government entity may seek declaratory judgment in a court of proper jurisdiction pursuant to a land use decision.
(Code 2011, § 42-41)

1132:
(a) Except as specifically defined herein, all words used in this article shall be as defined in the most recent edition of The Illustrated Book of Development Definitions (1993, Rutgers). Words not defined herein or in the above book shall be construed to have the meaning given by common and ordinary use and shall be interpreted within the context of the sentence, section, and article in which they occur.
(1) Words used in the singular include the plural and words used in the plural include the singular.
(2) Words used in the present tense include the future tense.
(3) The word "erected" includes the words "constructed," "moved," "located" or "relocated".
(4) The word "lot" includes the word "plot" or "parcel."
(5) The word "map" or "zoning map" means the zoning map of the City of Cochran, Georgia.
(6) The word "person" includes the words "individuals", "firms", "partnerships", "corporations", "associations", "governmental bodies" and all other legal entities.
(7) The word "shall" is always mandatory and never discretionary.
(8) The words "used" or occupied include the words "intended, arranged or designed to be used or occupied."
(9) For the purpose of this article, certain words or terms used herein shall be defined as follows:
Aggregate sign area means the combined sign surface area of all signs on a lot, excluding the area of one face of all double-faced signs. Noncommercial flags and banners are excluded from any determination of aggregate sign area.
Building means any structure attached to the ground which has a roof, and which is designed for the shelter, housing or enclosure of persons, animals, or property of any kind.
Building space, gross means the sum of the gross horizontal areas of the several floors of a building from the exterior face of the exterior walls, or from the centerline of a wall separating two buildings but excluding any space where the floor to ceiling height is less than six feet.
Double faced sign means any sign which has two display areas against each other or where the interior angle formed by the display areas is 60 degrees or less, where one face is designed to be seen from one direction and the other face from another direction.
Ground sign height means the distance in vertical feet from the elevation of the adjacent dedicated public street, edge of pavement, to the highest point of the sign structure. For property with an elevation higher than the adjacent public street, the height shall be measured from ground level at base of sign to the highest point of the sign structure. The ground shall not be altered for the sole purpose of providing additional sign height.
Flag means any piece of fabric or other flexible material solely containing a distinctive design used as the symbol of a nation, as a signaling device or as a decoration.
Landscape strip means any land area located within the boundary of a lot and required to be set aside and used for landscaping upon which only limited encroachments are authorized.
Lot means any designated parcel, tract, or area of land established by plat, subdivision, or as otherwise permitted by law, to be separately owned, used, developed, or built upon.
Parkway means any divided or undivided classified roadway.
Planned commercial/office/industrial development means any contiguous area or subdivision of land, planned and maintained as a single entity and containing one or more structures to accommodate retail, service, commercial, office or industrial uses, or a combination of such uses, and appurtenant common areas and accessory uses incidental to the predominant uses. (i.e., office park, shopping center, industrial park).
Principal use means the primary or predominant purpose for which a lot is occupied and/or used.
Road frontage means the distance on which a parcel of land adjoins a public street or public road right-of-way dedicated to and accepted by the City of Cochran for vehicular traffic or over which the City of Cochran may hold a prescriptive easement for public access including designated and numbered U.S. and state highways.
Sign means any object, device, display, or structure, or part thereof, which is used to advertise, identify, display, direct, or attract attention to an object, person, institution, organization, business, product, service, event, or location by any means, including words, letters, figures, design, symbols, fixtures, colors, illumination, artwork, or projected images. Any sign provided for in any zoning district may contain commercial or noncommercial messages.
Sign, animated means any sign, visible from the street, of which all or part thereof visibly moves or imitates movement in any fashion whatsoever; and any sign which contains or uses for illumination any light(s) or lighting device(s) which change color, flash or alternate, show movement or motion, or change the appearance of said sign or any part thereof automatically, excluding variable message boards.
Sign, banner means a piece of fabric or similar material that is attached to a pole, enclosed in a frame, or mounted as a temporary sign device.
Sign, billboard: See Outdoor advertising sign.
Sign, canopy: See Wall sign.
Sign, entrance means any permanent sign located at the public street or private driveway entrance to a residential development, residential subdivision development or nonresidential subdivision development.
Sign face means the area or display surface of a sign that is used for the message.
Sign, flashing: See Animated sign.
Sign, ground means any permanently affixed sign which is wholly independent of a building for support.
Sign, historic character mural means any sign that is painted on or applied to and made integral with a wall or surface of a building or structure.
Sign, indirectly illuminated means any sign illuminated by an external light source directed primarily toward such sign.
Sign, internally illuminated means any sign that emits light, illuminated by an internal light source.
Sign, off-premises means any sign which advertises or directs attention to property for sale, lease, or rent other than on the premises on which the sign is located.
Sign, monument means any permanent ground sign designed so that the base of the sign face is flush with the supporting base, and the supporting base is flush with the ground and extends the full width of the sign face.
Sign, multi-faced means any sign structure with more than two sign faces situated so that each sign face is facing a different direction.
Sign, non-conforming means any sign lawfully existing on the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, or amendment thereto that renders such sign non-conforming because it does not conform to all the standards and regulations of the adopted or amended ordinance.
Sign, outdoor advertising means a structural poster panel or painted sign, either free standing or attached to a building for the purpose of conveying information, knowledge, or ideas to the public about a subject unrelated to the premises upon which it is located. Also known as a billboard sign.
Sign, oversized or billboard sign: See Outdoor advertising sign.
Sign, pole means a sign that is mounted on a freestanding pole or similar support such that the bottom of the sign face is at least six feet above the ground.
Sign, portable means any sign which is manifestly designed to be transported, including by trailer or on its own wheels, even though the wheels of such sign may be removed, and the remaining chassis or support constructed without wheels is converted to an "A" or "T" frame sign or attached temporarily or permanently to the ground.
Sign, projecting means any sign projecting more than six inches from the outside wall or walls of any building upon which it is located.
Sign, roof means any sign projecting over the coping of a flat roof, or wholly or partially over the ridge of a gable, hip, or gambrel roof, and supported by or attached to said roof.
Sign, sidewalk or sandwich board means any moveable sign not secured or attached to the ground or surface upon which it is located.
Sign, streamer: See Portable sign.
Sign structure means the poles, beams, columns, posts, foundations, or other means providing structural support for the sign surface area to which the sign is affixed.
Sign surface area means the smallest square, rectangle, triangle, circle, or combination thereof, which encompasses the entire advertising area excluding architectural trim and structural supports.
Sign, subdivision directional means an off-premises sign that provides directions to property for sale, lease or rent. Subdivision directional signs are placed at intersections, directing traffic to a specific project(s).
Sign, temporary means a sign of a nonpermanent nature.
Sign, trailer: See Portable sign.
Sign, variable message means any programmable sign that is capable of changing the position or format or other displays on the sign face or change the visible display of words, numbers, symbols, and graphics by the use of a matrix of electric lamps, movable discs, movable panels, light apertures, or other methods; provided these changes are actuated by either a control mechanism or manually on the face of the sign. The display of changing information shall provide a minimum static duration of eight seconds for each display and a maximum transition time of two seconds between messages (i.e., digital, and electronic reader boards).
Sign, wall means any sign painted, applied to, or mounted to the wall or surface of a building or structure, the display surface, which does not project more than six inches from the outside wall of such a building or structure.
Sign, weekend directional means an off-premises sign that provides directions to property for sale, lease or rent. Weekend directional signs may be erected from Friday 3:00 p.m. until Sunday 11:59 p.m., and direct traffic to a specific project.
Sign, window display means any sign installed flush with the interior or exterior of a window and intended to be viewed from the outside.
Structure means anything constructed or erected on the ground or attached to something on the ground.
Yard, front means an open, unoccupied space on the same lot with a principal building or use, extending the full width of the lot and located between the street line and the front line of the building projected parallel to the street to the side lines of the lot. Corner lots shall be considered to have two front yards.
Yard, rear means an open space on the same lot with a principal building or use, unoccupied except by an accessory building or use, extending the full width of the lot and located between the rear line of the lot and the rear line of the building or use projected to the side lines of the lot.
Yard, side means an open, unoccupied space on the same lot with a principal building or use, located between the building or use and the sideline of the lot and extending from the rear line of the front yard to the front line of the rear yard.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Authorized private receptacle means a litter storage and collection receptacle as required and authorized in the city.
Garbage means animal and vegetable waste resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking, and residue of food and like matter, and similar items normally placed in household waste containers.
Handbill means any printed or written matter, any sample, device, circular, leaflet, pamphlet, newspaper, magazine, paper, booklet, or any other printed or otherwise reproduced original or copies of any matter of literature.

Public place means any and all streets, sidewalks, boulevards, alleys or other public ways, and any and all public parks, squares, spaces, grounds, and buildings.

(a) The city manager will report to the council at least once each year as to the problems encountered regarding solid waste, and whether the city should consider changes to improve administration. (g) Dangerous materials or substances, such as poisons, acids, caustics, infectious materials, batteries, explosives, paint, solvents, pesticides, herbicides, paint removers, petroleum products, petroleum by-products, etc., will not be collected by the city. (h) The collection of heavy dead animals, such as cows, horses, mules, etc., is not included in the services provided by the city. The owner or person having charge thereof will dispose of same in the manner and by the method directed by the city. The owner will be responsible for paying all charges.
(i) Materials not prepared for collection in accordance with regulations and rules shall not be collected by the city.
(j) Ashes will not be collected by the city.
(k) Barbershops, beauty salons, pet grooming salons, etc., shall not receive collection for discarded hair, unless the same is packaged in closed plastic bags and placed inside authorized garbage containers.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-29)
1169:
The collection of wastes resulting from manufacturing, assembling, processing, and other industrial operations, waste oils, and other similar materials from garages and filling stations, and the accumulation from packing houses, killing and dressing establishments, and wholesale fruit and vegetable houses shall not be included in the services provided by the city. Such premises or places shall dispose of same at their own expense in the manner and method directed by the landfill superintendent or appropriate state and local laws.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-30)
1170:
(a) The property owner and/or contractor in charge of a construction site shall furnish litter containers for construction and workers' litter. All litter from construction activity or any related activities shall be containerized and all litter will be picked up and placed in containers by workers at the end of each work day.
(b) Rocks, waste building materials, and other refuse resulting from building or remodeling operations or resulting from general cleanup of vacant or improved property just prior to occupancy will not be collected by the city.
(c) All such litter and waste shall be removed by the building contractor, owner, or occupant of the building at his own expense.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-31)
1171:
(a) The owner, occupant, or lessee of all property is required to remove all litter and place same in a proper container for collection. Vacant lots, borders, embankments, parking lots, storage lots, fences, walls, and sidewalks are to be kept free of litter. Parking lots, shopping centers, convenience stores, drive-in restaurants, and all commercial and industrial enterprises will ensure that no litter remains on their property.
(b) The city may remove litter from property where the owner/tenant refuses to do so and assess the cost for the cleanup against the property owner. Un-mowed, trashy, littered yards or landscapes may be cleaned if the city determines such a need and does not get a response in a timely manner from the owner/resident. A fine may be imposed in addition to actual cleanup costs.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-32)
1172:
The following items shall not be disposed of in city-provided containers, including, but not limited to, dumpsters, automated carts, and similar containers, nor will containers be emptied by the city until such items are removed:
(1) Household or industrial appliances. (The city will remove white metal household appliances if properly placed by a resident's automated refuse cart.)
(2) Furniture.
(3) Tires, paint, solvents, or other chemicals. (Tires may be taken to the county landfill by the owner and disposed of with the owner paying a disposal fee.)
(4) Wooden crates.
(5) Logs and limbs.
(6) Bed springs.
(7) Rocks, dirt, or concrete blocks.
(8) Mattresses.
(9) Liquids, wet garbage, food scraps, etc., of any type not sealed in appropriate containers.
(10) Construction materials, including roofing materials.
(11) Ashes and burned materials.
(12) Yard debris, including grass clippings.
(13) Hypodermic needles, hospital and medical waste, or infectious or toxic substances (potentially or actually).
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-33)
1173:
(a) The city will review and approve all plans and specifications for the installation of compactor units to be used in connection with containers to this section. Such compactors will be approved by the city prior to installation being made. All compactor shredders and compactor containers shall be installed on Class A, 3,000-pound-per-square-inch concrete pads of not less than a six-inch thickness. All such installations shall comply with the requirements of the building code of the city, the fire prevention code, and other safety laws and ordinances of the city council. The city is authorized to adopt regulations as may be necessary with reference to such matters.
(b) Compactors will be served by the city's authorized representatives.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-34)
1174:
(a) The following provisions are made for any resident who cannot use automated refuse carts, provided the following requirements are met:
(1) The handicapped, disabled, or elderly/feeble resident must live alone or all persons living at that household must also be disabled.
(2) Disability forms provided by the city must be completed by the resident's physician and returned to the city. If more than one person lives in the household, disability forms must be completed for each person living therein.
(b) If the requirements pursuant to subsection (a) of this section are not met, an automated refuse cart will be delivered to the resident and regular service will be provided by the city.
(c) The city will provide special service to those residents who meet this requirement, provided that such residents help by placing their household refuse near the front or side of their home in an easily reachable location, and provided that the refuse is contained in closed, durable plastic bags. Refuse must be placed for collection by 7:30 a.m. on the designated collection days.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-35)
1175:
Fees for garbage collection shall be in the amount established by the city council from time to time.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-36)
1176:
All holders of tree services licenses or any person engaging in the cutting of trees, to include landscaping services for a fee paid by the owner or resident of a property, shall first be required to notify the public works department, giving the location and date of the cutting or lawn care proposed to be done, as well as the estimated amount of debris which will result. The public works department will not be responsible for collection of debris except upon request and payment of a fee per load plus disposal charges, where applicable. The amount of the collection fee shall be in an amount as established by the city council from time to time.
(Ord. of 5-14-2013(2), § 48-37)
1177:
Vacant properties, including properties not paying for city utilities, yard trash, bulk waste, or construction debris on the right-of-way of a vacant property not billed by the city, shall be governed by the following:
(1) Code enforcement will identify owner. If owner is identified, they will verbally be given three days to remove the material. If owner does not remove all material, then city public works will arrange to remove the remaining material through the city work-order system, according to the following schedule:
$50.00 per 125 cubic feet (5' x 5' x 5') of material; tires are charged $10 per tire. If property owner fails to pay, then their bill will be referred to Darnell Services, the city's utility collection agency.
If owner cannot be identified, then city will arrange to pick up material as soon as possible, and impose a lien on the property.
(2) Vacant properties with illegal dumping on private property. Code enforcement will contact the owner and enforce illegal dumping through the nuisance ordinance.
(3) Mixed piles—Yard waste, bulk waste and construction debris.
a. Advanced disposal will not pick up mixed piles.
b. Mixed piles in front of properties with city utilities will be handled by public works.
c. Mixed piles in front of vacant properties will be handled by code enforcement.
Code enforcement will identify owner of the property with the mixed pile. If owner is identified, they will verbally be given three days to remove the mixed pile. If owner does not remove all the mixed pile, then city public works will arrange to remove the remaining mixed pile through the city work-order system, according to the following schedule:
$50.00 per 125 cubic feet (5' x 5' x 5') of mixed pile; tires are charged $10 per tire. If property owner fails to pay, then their bill will be referred to Darnell Services, the city's utility collection agency.
If owner cannot be identified, then city will arrange to pick up material as soon as possible, and impose a lien on the property.
(4) Large quantities of yard debris or stumps in the right-of-way.
a. If a contractor is found responsible, then code enforcement will be notified and the contractor or owner will be given three days to remove the yard debris, or the city will arrange to remove the remaining debris through the city work-order schedule according to a rate of $50.00 per 125 cubic feet.
b. If a homeowner is found responsible, then large quantities of yard debris or stumps will be referred to public works to arrange for the disposal of the material over a period of time.
(5) Bulk waste furniture, household items.
a. Bulk waste piles in front of properties with city utilities will be picked up by advanced disposal the second Saturday of every month. Property owners should put out bulk waste no earlier than the week prior to the scheduled Saturday pick-up. Code enforcement will become involved with bulk waste piles that are placed in the city right-of-way other than the week of pick-up (second Saturday of every month).
NOTE: The charges above are listed as $50.00 per 125 cubic feet of material and $10.00 per tire.
(Ord. of 1-14-2020(1))
1180:
(a) Initially, the city will issue an automated refuse cart to each occupied residence on each automated route at no charge. The cart is the property of the city and shall not be removed from the address if the resident should move. A cart identification number will be assigned to the resident's utility account.
(b) The cart shall only be removed from the property by duly authorized personnel of the sanitation department.
(c) If the cart is stolen, the resident shall report the theft to the police department and the sanitation department. After receipt of the police report, the sanitation department will replace the automated cart at minimal charge to the resident.
(d) The sanitation department is tasked to maintain automated carts in good working condition upon notification by the customers that repairs are needed.
(e) If one automated cart is not sufficient for the household garbage generated, additional carts may be requested from the sanitation department. The fee will be the current basic sanitation rate times the number of carts issued to each address.
(f) Each residence must have its own garbage container. Sharing of containers by multiple residences is not permitted.
(g) Commercial customers using automated refuse carts will not allow any other business or household to use their containers.
(h) Abuse of city-owned containers may result in a fine.
(Code 2011, § 48-61; Ord. of 1995, § 12.0)
1181:
(a) Automated refuse carts shall be placed immediately adjacent to the street for collection only on designated collection days.
(b) Carts shall be placed at the proper location for collection by 7:30 a.m. on designated collection days and shall be removed from the street by 7:00 p.m. on the same day. A written notice may be issued which may result in a fine for noncompliance with this section. After one written notice is issued to remove a cart from the street, a fine in the amount set by the city council will be imposed for any subsequent violations of this requirement.
(c) Carts shall not be placed within four feet of any obstacle such as mailboxes, trash, trees, yard waste, white metal appliances, carts in driveway, etc.
(d) Carts shall be placed no more than three feet away from the street.
(e) Carts shall be placed with the identification number facing the street.
(f) Cars parked on the street must be at least 50 feet away from the cart.
(g) Carts shall be serviced once each week, except in some instances when a holiday occurs and the city provides an alternate schedule for pick-up, which will normally be published in the paper beforehand and will always be available at city hall. Equipment failure may also alter the schedule.
(h) Unless this section is complied with, the city may not provide service to the container.
(Code 2011, § 48-62; Ord. of 1995, § 13.0)
1182:
(a) Garbage may be placed in automated refuse carts if properly prepared and deposited as defined herein.
(b) Refuse may be placed inside an automated refuse cart, provided that such trash fits inside the cart without hindering the free flow of refuse from the cart when it is emptied.
(c) An automated cart shall not be overfilled so that the lid does not close properly. If there is overflow garbage, on rare occasions, such overflow garbage shall be properly bagged and placed next to the automated refuse cart, but no closer than four feet from any obstacle such as mailboxes, trash, trees, yard waste, white metal appliances, carts in driveway, etc.
(Code 2011, § 48-63; Ord. of 1995, § 14.0)
1183:
Items enumerated in this article as unacceptable for city containers shall not be placed in a refuse cart. A container containing unacceptable refuse shall not be emptied until such time as the items are removed from the cart. A fine in the amount set by the city council shall be imposed on any person violating this section.
(Code 2011, § 48-64; Ord. of 1995, § 15.0)
1186:
No person shall throw or deposit litter in or upon any street, sidewalk or other public place within the city except in public receptacles or in authorized private receptacles for collection.
(Code 1999, § 6-702; Code 2011, § 48-120)
1187:
Persons placing litter in public receptacles or in authorized private receptacles shall do so in such a manner as to prevent it from being carried or deposited by the elements upon any street, sidewalk or other public place or upon private property.
(Code 1999, § 6-703; Code 2011, § 48-121)
1188:
No person shall sweep into or deposit in any gutter, street or other public place within the city the accumulation of litter from any building or lot or from any public or private sidewalk or driveway. Persons owning or occupying property shall keep the sidewalk in front of their premises free of litter.
(Code 1999, § 6-704; Code 2011, § 48-122)
1189:
No person owning or occupying a place of business shall sweep into or deposit in any gutter, street or other public place within the city the accumulation of litter from any building or lot or from any public or private sidewalk or driveway. Persons owning or occupying places of business within the city shall keep the sidewalk in front of their business premises free of litter.
(Code 1999, § 6-705; Code 2011, § 48-123)
1190:
No person, while a driver or passenger in a vehicle, shall throw or deposit litter upon any street or other public place within the city, or upon private property.
(Code 1999, § 6-706; Code 2011, § 48-124)
1191:
No person shall drive or move any truck or other vehicle within the city unless such vehicle is so constructed or loaded as to prevent any load, contents or litter from being blown or deposited upon any street, alley or other public place. Nor shall any person drive or move any vehicle or truck within the city, the wheels or tires of which carry onto or deposit in any street, alley or other public place, mud, dirt, sticky substances, litter or foreign matter of any kind.
(Code 1999, § 6-707; Code 2011, § 48-125)
1192:
No person shall throw or deposit litter in any park within the city except in public receptacles and in such a manner that the litter will be prevented from being carried or deposited by the elements upon any part of the park or upon any street or other public place. Where public receptacles are not provided, all such litter shall be carried away from the park by the person responsible for its presence and properly disposed of elsewhere as provided herein.
(Code 1999, § 6-708; Code 2011, § 48-126)
1193:
No person shall throw or deposit litter into any fountain, pond, lake, stream, or any other body of water in a park or elsewhere within the city.
(Code 1999, § 6-709; Code 2011, § 48-127)
1194:
No person shall throw or deposit any commercial or noncommercial handbill in or upon any sidewalk, street or other public place within the city.
(Code 1999, § 6-710; Code 2011, § 48-128)
1195:
No person shall throw or deposit litter on any occupied private property within the city, whether owned by such person or not, except that the owner or person in control of private property may maintain authorized private receptacles for collection in such a manner that litter will be prevented from being carried or deposited by the elements upon any street, sidewalk or other public place or upon any private property.
(Code 1999, § 6-711; Code 2011, § 48-129)
1196:
The owner or person in control of any private property shall at all times maintain the premises free of litter. Provided, however, that this section shall not prohibit the storage of litter in authorized private receptacles for collection.
(Code 1999, § 6-712; Code 2011, § 48-130)
1197:
No person shall throw or deposit litter on any open or vacant private property within the city whether owned by such person or not.
(Code 1999, § 6-713; Code 2011, § 48-131)
1198:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Damaging public property, O.C.G.A. § 16-7-25; governmental authorization for construction or maintenance of any private road unlawful, O.C.G.A. § 32-1-8; state, county and municipal road systems, O.C.G.A. § 32-4-1 et seq.; municipal road systems, O.C.G.A. § 32-4-90 et seq.; regulation of maintenance and use of public roads generally, O.C.G.A. § 32-6-1 et seq.; municipal authority to grant right to erect obstructions in streets, O.C.G.A. § 36-30-10; enclosures of lanes or alleys, O.C.G.A. § 36-30-11; municipal street improvements, O.C.G.A. § 36-39-1 et seq.
1202:
It shall be unlawful for any property owner or occupant to have or maintain on his property any tree, hedge, billboard, or other obstruction which prevents persons driving vehicles on public streets or alleys from obtaining a clear view of traffic when approaching an intersection.
(Code 1999, § 6-1001; Code 2011, § 50-19)
1203:
It shall be unlawful for any person to place or have placed any banner or sign across any public street or alley except when expressly authorized by the mayor.
(Code 1999, § 6-1002; Code 2011, § 50-20)
1204:
It shall be unlawful for any person to permit or cause the obstruction of any drainage ditch in any public right-of-way.
(Code 1999, § 6-1003; Code 2011, § 50-21)
1205:
The occupants of property abutting on a sidewalk are required to keep the sidewalk clean. Also, immediately after a snow or sleet, such occupants are required to remove all accumulated snow or ice from the abutting sidewalk.
(Code 1999, § 6-1004; Code 2011, § 50-22)
1206:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to build or maintain within the fire limits of the city over or upon the sidewalks or streets of said city, within said limits, any shelter or sidewalk or street covering, which shall encroach upon said streets or sidewalks, which said shelter or sidewalk or street covering shall be supported from the ground by columns or otherwise.
(b) No awning shall be built or maintained over the sidewalks of the city, within the fire limits, which shall approach nearer to the ground or pavement than seven feet; and no such awning shall be constructed without a permit from the city council first obtained, and upon application, giving details of construction.
(c) Any party who shall build or maintain any shelter, awning, or covering in violation of this section shall be punished as provided for in section 1-15.
(d) In any case of violation of the provisions of this section, the city, through its officers, shall have the right to remove any shelter, awning, or covering built or maintained in violation of this section at the expense of the person responsible for such violation, where such person fails to remove such shelter, awning, or covering within five days after notice for removal shall be given by the city.
(Code 1999, § 6-1011; Code 2011, § 50-23; Ord. of 11-21-1922)
1207:
It shall be unlawful for any person to deface any public sidewalk, street, or curb in the city by painting any signs thereon, whether for commercial advertising purposes or not, or to walk or drive any vehicle upon or injure in any way any newly laid street, sidewalk, or curbing pavement while the same is guarded by a warning sign or barricade or is soft or newly laid.
(Code 2011, § 50-24)
1208:
It shall be unlawful for any person to ride any horse or any vehicle on any city sidewalks. Any person violating this section shall be deemed guilty of disorderly conduct.
(Code 2011, § 50-25)
1209:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit on any street or sidewalk any rubbish or any material that may be harmful to the pavement thereof, or any waste material, or any glass or other article that may do injury to any person, animal, or property.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge or to allow to be discharged onto any public street or sidewalk any water or other fluid material containing objectionable material such as sewage, waste, milk, or other organic material. Thus, it shall be unlawful for anyone to wash automobiles on the city sidewalks.
(Code 2011, § 50-26)
1210:
It shall be unlawful for any person to use any street, sidewalk, or other public place as space for the display of goods or merchandise for sale, or to write or make any sign or advertisement on any such pavement, unless approved by the mayor.
(Code 2011, § 50-27)
1211:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, or corporation to burn any leaves, paper, rubbish, or other substances upon any of the public streets, sidewalks, or alleys of the city.
(Code 2011, § 50-28)
1212:
Any person laying or repairing any pavement on a street, sidewalk, or other public place shall maintain suitable barricades to prevent injury to any person or vehicle by reason of the work, which barricades shall be protected by a light at nighttime.
(Code 2011, § 50-29)
1213:
(a) All persons who own real estate in the city which abuts upon any sidewalk which is paved shall be required to keep that portion of such sidewalk which lies between the property line and the curbline of the adjoining street, and upon which his real estate abuts, in good and smooth condition and free from growing weeds and other obnoxious and unsightly vegetation or other things which would mar or detract from the beauty and cleanliness of the street upon which his property abuts.
(b) Any property owner who shall place or allow grass to grow upon the portion of sidewalk lying between the property line and the curbline of the street as aforesaid, and upon which his real estate abuts, shall keep such grass properly mowed and free from rubbish of all kinds. If such owner is not in the possession of his property, then this section shall apply to his tenants or those who have possession or control of the same.
(Code 2011, § 50-30)
1214:
It shall be the duty of every city officer and employee who becomes aware of any defect or obstruction, or of any unlawful deposit or discharge, in or on any public street, alley, curb, sidewalk, or other public way of the city to report the same as soon as possible.
(Code 2011, § 50-31)
1215:
It shall be unlawful for any person to construct or maintain any opening or stairway in any public street, sidewalk, or alley without first obtaining a permit from the city clerk in the manner specified in this article. All such lawfully maintained openings shall be guarded by a suitable strong cover or railing approved by the street superintendent.
(Code 2011, § 50-32)
1216:
Any person or company which maintains poles and wires in the streets, alleys, or other public places of the city shall keep such wires and poles free and away from any nearby trees or shrubs in such places, and keep all such trees and shrubs properly trimmed, subject to the supervision of the designated city official, so that no injury shall befall either the poles and wires or the shrubs and trees by their contact.
(Code 2011, § 50-33)
1219:
Upon petition as provided in this article, the city will pay one-half and the affected property owners shall pay one-half of the total cost of installation of sidewalks, curbs and gutters, but only if adequate funds are in the treasury of the city to cover the city's portion of the cost of the project as determined by the city council.
(Code 2011, § 50-55)
1220:
Costs of construction shall be prorated among the affected property owners by taking one-half of the total of the improvement made and prorating the cost thereof on the property owners according to their frontage on the sidewalks and curbs and gutters so improved.
(Code 2011, § 50-56)
1224:
(a) No number of persons shall block any street, sidewalk, alley or entrance to any place of business in the city by congregating on any street, alley, sidewalk, or entrance to any place of business in said city in such number as to interfere with traffic or the conduct of business thereon and therein; not more than four persons shall congregate at any one point on Second Street from the First Baptist Church to Southern Railway Crossing with North Second Street, in any one block, either in the street or on either sidewalk along said street.
(b) No number of persons shall congregate in any place of business in said city in such a number as will interfere with the conduct of business therein, nor shall any person remain in said place of business when requested by the owner, manager or person in charge thereof to leave the premises.
(c) No person shall sit down or lie down in any street, alley, sidewalk, or place of business in said city.
(d) No person shall fail or refuse to cease and desist from any such violation when ordered to do so by any peace officer, or the owner, manager or person in charge of any place of business in said city.
(Code 1999, § 6-1010; Code 2011, § 50-77; Ord. of 9-3-1963)
1227:
It shall be unlawful to hold any parade, demonstration or congregation of people on the streets, alleys and sidewalks of the city without first obtaining a written permit therefor from the state department of transportation, if it is to be held on a state highway, and from the city mayor and chief of police, if it is to be held on a city street. Before any such permit shall be granted, the person desiring to hold any parade, demonstration or congregation of people on said streets, alleys or sidewalks shall make written application to said city council for a permit therefor, and in such application it shall be stated the number of persons to be engaged in same, the number and character of vehicles to be used in same, the place from which same shall start, the route to be taken and the end of same, together with the approximate time of holding such parade, demonstration or congregation, when the same shall start, and when the same will end.
(Code 1999, § 6-1005; Code 2011, § 50-98; Ord. of 9-3-1963, § 1)
1228:
When a parade application is submitted, the city manager and chief of police shall consider same as to whether such activity applied for shall work an undue burden on the traffic and business of the city or shall block or interfere with business or traffic in the city. The city manager and chief of police shall grant or refuse same or fix the time of starting, the place of starting, the route to be followed, the end of same and the amount of time to be consumed in such activity. If the permit is granted by the city manager and chief of police, such activity shall proceed under the terms of the permit. If the permit is refused by the city manager or chief of police, no such parade, demonstration or congregation shall be held.
(Code 1999, § 6-1006; Code 2011, § 50-99; Ord. of 9-3-1963, § 2; Amend. of 9-8-2020)
1229:
Any parade, demonstration or congregation of people held in the city pursuant to a permit granted by the mayor and chief of police as herein provided shall be conducted in an orderly manner. In the event any such activity shall not be so conducted, the city shall immediately order the activity discontinued. Failure or refusal of any person engaged in such activity to disperse and cease when ordered to do so shall subject the person to penalties as provided in section 1-15.
(Code 1999, § 6-1007; Code 2011, § 50-100; Ord. of 9-3-1963, § 3)
1232:
The purpose of this article is to set minimum standards for streets and roadways to be accepted into the city road system so as to provide for the public economy, safety and orderly traffic flow and movement, and for other purposes.
(Code 2011, § 50-129; Ord. of 1996, § I)
1233:
This article shall apply to streets and roads constructed and built by individuals and developers who propose to induce the city to accept such streets and roadways into the public transportation system of the city. This article shall not work to restrict the city from constructing its own roadways and streets in any instance and at any location wherein such construction is in the interest of the public and for enlarging, increasing or improving the flow of traffic and to provide needed accesses for ingress and egress for public purposes.
(Code 2011, § 50-130; Ord. of 1996, § II)
1234:
The city shall not automatically accept streets and roadways constructed in compliance with the minimum conditions provided for hereunder, unless it can be reasonably expected and shown that such streets will be utilized for public purposes. Such use will be of public significance and the acceptance of same will not work to defeat the public economy by requiring maintenance and upkeep in a disproportionate amount to the public good created by such acceptance.
(Code 2011, § 50-131; Ord. of 1996, § III)
1235:
The owner of such property seeking to induce the city to accept same shall certify this conveyance to be his free act and deed and will dedicate same to the public use forever all such streets, alleys, and easements, without restriction or reversion.
(Code 2011, § 50-132; Ord. of 1996, § III)
1236:
Any property so conveyed under the provisions hereof to the city shall be accompanied by a recordable plat depicting the finished streets and rights-of-way and at a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet, and which plat shall show, in case of a subdivision, the boundaries of said subdivision; the names of such streets or roadways; the names and record owners of any adjoining unplatted land in the case of a subdivision; the easements for public utilities; the location of existing roads or streets which adjoin or abut the streets or roadways proposed to be conveyed to the city; and those streets or roadways which extend to within 80 feet of the streets or roadways proposed to be conveyed to the city.
(Code 2011, § 50-133; Ord. of 1996, § IV)
1237:
(a) Any property conveyance to the city pursuant to this article shall be accompanied by a recordable plat depicting, at a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet:
(1) The names and locations of finished streets and rights-of-way.
(2) The names and locations of existing roads or streets that adjoin or abut the streets or roadways proposed to be conveyed to the city.
(3) The names and locations of those streets and roadways that extend to within 80 feet of the streets or roadways proposed to be conveyed to the city.
(4) The locations of all easements for public utilities.
(5) If the property conveyed is located in a subdivision, the boundaries of the subdivision and the names of record owners of any adjoining unplatted land.
(b) No streets or roadways shall be accepted by the city unless same are paved at the time of such proposed conveyance to the city and which paving meets the minimum standards as provided for herein. The entire cost of such construction, grading, drainage, sloping, grassing, engineering, surveying and all other expenses shall be at the sole cost and expense of such developer or subdivider.
(Code 2011, § 50-134; Ord. of 1996, § V)
1238:
(a) Minimum right-of-way widths for acceptance of city streets are as follows:
Expressways | 200 feet
Arterial streets | 100 feet
Connector streets | 80 feet
Minor streets:
| Residential | 50 feet
| Commercial and industrial | 70 feet
| Cul-de-sacs and loop streets | 50 feet
| Turn-around (diameter) | 100 feet
| Marginal access or frontage roads | 40 feet
Alleys, service drives and private drives | 22 feet
(b) In addition, street intersections shall be as nearly at right angles as possible, and no intersection shall be at an angle less than 75 degrees.
(Code 2011, § 50-135; Ord. of 1996, § VI)
1239:
(a) Grading. All streets, roads and alleys shall be graded by the subdivider to provide the necessary paving, roadway, drainage, and safety requirements.
